lead.t: Fistula-in-ano → external opening with pus/granulation tissue near anus
lead.s: CNS & Abdominal Exam: Clinical Techniques, History & Neurology — Notes

b: Definition. An abnormal tract between the anal canal (internal opening at the dentate line) and the perianal skin (external opening). It is nearly always the result of a previous anorectal abscess, so patients present with recurrent dischar
Other causes: Crohn's disease, tuberculosis, trauma, anal fissure, cancer, radiotherapy, actinomycosis, chlamydia, HIV and other immunosuppression.

Practical grouping: low (superficial, intersphincteric, low transsphincteric) fistulae are simple; high transsphincteric, suprasphincteric, extrasphincteric, multiple or recurrent fistulae are complex .

Goodsall's rule. A fistula with its external opening anterior to a transverse line through the anus runs a straight radial course to the dentate line. One with its external opening posterior to the line runs a curved course to the posterior

Clinical features. Intermittent or constant perianal discharge (commonest), pain relieved when pus drains, perianal swelling, bleeding, skin irritation, an external opening with granulation tissue and an indurated cord felt under the skin o

qs.q: A 28-year-old man with a history of recurrent perianal discharge is examined for a fistula-in-ano. The external opening is located anterior to a transverse line drawn through the anus. According to Goodsall's rule, what course does the fistula tract typically follow?
o: A curved course leading to the posterior midline
An upward course over the puborectalis muscle
A circumferential spread within the intersphincteric plane
A straight radial course directly to the dentate line
qs.e: Goodsall's rule states that a fistula with an anterior external opening runs a straight radial course to the dentate line. Posterior openings typically follow a curved course to the posterior midline.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: A 45-year-old woman with Crohn's disease presents with a high transsphincteric fistula-in-ano. To preserve continence, which initial surgical intervention is most appropriate?
qs.e: A draining seton is the standard initial management for complex or Crohn's-associated fistulae to maintain drainage and protect sphincter function. Immediate fistulotomy is contraindicated in high fistulae due to the high risk of incontinence.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old man undergoes surgery for a low intersphincteric fistula-in-ano. Which complication is most feared by surgeons performing anorectal operations?
qs.e: Faecal incontinence is the most feared complication following anorectal surgery due to potential injury to the anal sphincter mechanisms. Urinary retention is common but less feared.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: A 39-year-old woman with a low, simple intersphincteric fistula-in-ano undergoes definitive surgical treatment. Which procedure is performed for 85 to 95 percent of these simple fistulae?
o: Fistulotomy by laying open the tract
qs.e: Fistulotomy, or laying open the tract, is successful for 85 to 95% of simple, low fistulae. Fistulectomy creates larger wounds without offering a lower recurrence rate.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: What is the primary role of a cutting seton when managed in a patient with a fistula-in-ano?
o: To provide continuous passive drainage and prevent recurrent abscess formation
To completely excise the fibrotic tract and surrounding granulation tissue in one stage
To slowly cut through the muscle over several weeks while fibrosis keeps the sphincter in place
To seal the internal opening using biological glue and mechanical plugs
qs.e: A cutting seton is tightened gradually over 6 to 8 weeks to slowly cut through the muscle while fibrosis protects sphincter alignment. A loose seton is used strictly for drainage.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old man is investigated for a recurrent, complex fistula-in-ano. Which imaging modality is considered the best test to map the anatomy of this condition?
qs.e: MRI is the best test for complex or recurrent fistulae to accurately delineate tracts and secondary collections. Fistulography is an older, less accurate modality.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: During the examination of a patient under anaesthesia for a suspected fistula-in-ano, what diagnostic adjunct is commonly used alongside a probe to identify the internal opening?
qs.e: Methylene blue or hydrogen peroxide can be injected to help identify the internal opening during examination under anaesthesia. Barium is used for radiological contrast studies.
qs.s: Benign Anorectal Disorders: Haemorrhoids, Anal Fissure, Anorectal: MCQs

qs.q: According to Parks classification of fistula-in-ano, which anatomical course describes a suprasphincteric fistula?
o: Up and over the puborectalis, then down to the skin
Crosses both sphincters into the ischiorectal fossa
Between internal and external sphincters to perianal skin
Outside sphincters through the levator ani into rectum
qs.e: A suprasphincteric fistula travels up and over the puborectalis muscle before descending down to the skin. Intersphincteric tracts stay between the two sphincters.
